Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the NovaRetail Q1 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. [Standard operator instructions on muting lines, repeating questions, etc.] I would now like to turn the call over to Emily Carter, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to NovaRetail's Q1 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Michael Reynolds, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; and David Patel, COO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Michael Reynolds, CEO of NovaRetail.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Emily, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q1 performance, driven by robust growth in our marketplace and early wins from AI-powered personalization efforts, alongside steady active customer expansion. Our trailing 12-month GMV reached impressive levels, reflecting the resilience of our platform amid a competitive landscape.

Our focus remains on optimizing product assortment toward higher-value categories and enhancing customer retention through loyalty programs. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our NovaMart AI Suite, which we believe will significantly boost conversion rates and basket sizes through advanced recommendation capabilities.

Finally, we are committed to driving fulfillment efficiencies and navigating supply chain challenges to protect margins. These initiatives position us well for sustained growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Michael. Our Q1 revenue was $4.1 billion, an increase of 12% year-over-year. Gross margin was 45.2%, driven by favorable product mix shifts and lower inbound freight costs relative to peers. Operating expenses were $1.6 billion, representing 39% of revenue, reflecting disciplined spend on marketing and tech investments.

Our net income for the quarter was $280 million, or $0.72 per share. We ended the quarter with $5.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. 

As we dive deeper into our key performance metrics, I'd like to spend a few minutes on Average Order Value, or AOV, trends and the factors driving changes. AOV remains a cornerstone of our profitability model in the e-commerce space, directly influencing gross margin expansion and customer lifetime value. For context, our trailing 12-month AOV stood at $92.50 in Q1 2024, up 8.2% year-over-year from $85.60 in Q1 2023, and sequentially up 2.1% from Q4 2023's $90.60. This marks our strongest quarterly AOV growth since Q2 2022, when pandemic-driven home essentials spending peaked.

Let me break this down by the primary drivers, which we've isolated through our internal cohort analysis and attribution modeling.

First, product mix shift toward higher-value categories, contributing about 45% to the AOV lift. Our AOV expansion has been fueled by a deliberate pivot in assortment strategy. Electronics and home & garden categories, which carry average ticket sizes of $185 and $142 respectively, now represent 28% of GMV—up from 22% a year ago—driven by strong demand for mid-tier consumer electronics like smart home devices and appliances amid hybrid work trends. Conversely, apparel and accessories, with sub-$65 AOVs, dipped to 35% of GMV from 41%, as we deprioritized low-margin fast fashion SKUs in favor of premium private-label lines, such as our NovaHome Essentials brand, which saw 15% AOV uplift from bundling kitchenware sets. This mirrors industry peers like Wayfair, where home category AOVs have climbed 12% YoY on similar premiumization plays.

Second, personalization and recommendation engine enhancements, contributing around 30% to the lift. On the tech side, our AI-driven recommendation engine, powered by a partnership with Adobe Sensei and our proprietary NovaRecs v2.0, has been a game-changer. Add-to-cart upsell acceptance rates improved to 24% in Q1 from 18% last year, adding about $6.20 to basket size per session. Cross-sell bundles—like pairing AirPods with iPhone cases or suggesting complementary beauty products via 'Shop the Look' carousels—boosted AOV by 11% for logged-in Prime-like subscribers, who now account for 62% of orders. We've A/B tested this across 15 million sessions, yielding a 3.2x ROI on our $25 million personalization CapEx spend in FY23. This is akin to Shopify merchants leveraging apps like Rebuy, where top performers report 10-15% AOV gains.

Third, loyalty and subscription program optimization, contributing roughly 15% to the lift. Our NovaPrime membership, with 18 million active subs up 22% YoY, continues to deliver outsized AOV at $118 versus $72 for non-members. Free shipping thresholds at $49—dynamically adjusted via ML algorithms—encouraged 14% more items per order, while exclusive perks like early access to limited-drop electronics drove 20% higher AOV during flash sales. We've also rolled out subscription-and-save models for consumables, like beauty refills à la Dollar Shave Club, capturing 8% of repeat orders with 25% AOV premiums.

Performance varied by geography, reflecting macro tailwinds and headwinds: North America, 65% of GMV, hit $102 AOV, +9.5% YoY, propelled by US consumer resilience in durables despite 3.5% inflation, though Canada lagged at +6% due to softer apparel demand. EMEA, 18% of GMV, reached $85 AOV, +7% YoY, with UK strength from Brexit-fueled domestic sourcing but Germany pressured by energy costs curbing impulse buys. APAC, 12% of GMV, was $78 AOV, +5% YoY, led by India’s JioMart integration boosting rural electronics bundles, offset by China's zero-COVID hangover and competition from Pinduoduo's group-buy low-AOV model. LatAm, 5% of GMV, was $65 AOV, flat YoY, as FX volatility in Brazil eroded pricing power.

Not all smooth sailing—aggressive discounting during Black Friday bleed-over reduced AOV by 4% in Q4 carryover cohorts, and rising ad costs shifted acquisition to lower-AOV mobile-only users (AOV $68 vs. desktop $110). We've countered with dynamic pricing via our Elastic Path CMS, capping promo depth at 25% for high-LTV segments, and geofencing high-AOV urban markets.

Looking ahead, we expect Q2 AOV of $94-$96, implying 6-8% YoY growth, supported by Q2 launches like AR virtual try-ons for fashion (piloted with 20% AOV lift in beta) and B2B wholesale bundles via our NovaPro portal. Long-term, we're targeting $110 AOV by FY26 through marketplace expansion—adding 5,000 third-party sellers vetted for $100+ AOV thresholds—and GenAI chat commerce, where early tests show 18% basket inflation. This positions us competitively against Amazon's $110+ Prime AOV and Walmart+'s push into higher-ticket groceries.

In summary, our AOV trajectory underscores disciplined execution on mix, tech, and retention amid a maturing e-commerce landscape where scale alone isn't enough—it's about basket intelligence.

Before turning to questions, let me address logistics and shipping costs, a key pressure point this quarter amid persistent supply chain disruptions. As a leading e-commerce platform with substantial GMV, serving millions of active customers across apparel, consumer electronics, and home goods, our fulfillment network is the backbone of our same-day and two-day delivery promises. This quarter, these costs rose 18% year-over-year to levels representing about 14.5% of net revenue—up from 12.2% last year and above our historical target of under 13%. This headwind shaved approximately 220 basis points off our adjusted EBITDA margin, but we're actively mitigating it through a multi-pronged strategy.

The perfect storm began with geopolitical flashpoints like the Red Sea crisis—stemming from Houthi attacks since late 2023—forcing a 40% rerouting of container ships around the Cape of Good Hope, adding 10-14 days to Asia-Europe and Asia-US East Coast transit times. This translated to a 25-30% spike in ocean freight spot rates from Shanghai to Los Angeles, peaking at $4,200 per FEU before moderating. For NovaRetail, this inflated inbound logistics for high-volume SKUs like electronics from Shenzhen, pushing average ocean freight cost per container up 28% YoY.

Compounding this, the Panama Canal drought restricted transits, bottlenecking imports, while air freight rates surged 15%. Domestically, port strikes delayed goods, and fuel surcharges added 300 basis points. Last-mile delivery faced urban congestion, with costs per package up 12%.

Regionally: North America saw 16% cost increases due to West Coast port dwell times up 22%; Europe ballooned 24% from customs and carbon levies; APAC and emerging markets rose 22%, though localization helped. Overall, inventory turns compressed, tying up working capital.

Broader trends show e-commerce logistics shifting structurally, with rising expedited shipping and carrier consolidation pressuring margins, offset by nearshoring.

Our countermeasures include AI-driven network optimization with PeakFlow AI dynamically rerouting shipments, reducing costs 9% QoQ; DC automation boosting efficiency 35%; supplier diversification shifting volume to Vietnam/India; and inventory resilience via ML demand sensing. These are tracking to strong ROI.

Looking ahead, we expect moderation in Q2, but monitor risks like tariffs. Strategically, we're leaning into omnichannel logistics, FBA-competitive services, and drone pilots.

Now, turning to forward guidance. Our outlook for Q2 2024 and full FY2024 remains constructive, underpinned by robust consumer demand in core categories; share gains; and payoffs from NovaMart AI Suite and Fulfillment Network 2.0. We're tempering modestly for FX headwinds, competition from Temu and Shein, and tariff risks.

For Q2 revenue, we expect $4.2 billion to $4.3 billion, 10% to 13% YoY growth, driven by take rates expanding to 22.5%, higher-margin first-party sales, and advertising up 25% YoY. North America $2.7B-$2.8B up 11%; Europe $0.8B-$0.85B +12%; APAC/LATAM $0.6B-$0.65B flat to +2% at constant FX.

Full FY2024 revenue guide: $16.5 billion to $17 billion, 14% to 16% growth, with AOV expansion and new categories like health subscriptions.

Q2 GMV $8.5B-$8.8B, +9-12% YoY, with marketplace at 75% mix. FY2024 GMV $115B-$120B, +13-16%.

Profitability: Q2 adjusted EBITDA $550M-$600M, 13-14% margins from gross stability, FCPO declines, OpEx discipline. FY2024 EBITDA $3.8B-$4.0B, 13.2-13.6% margins; FCF >$3B.

Our Marketplace Momentum strategy invests in AI, global fulfillment, sustainability. Monitoring macros, but positioned for durable growth.

We are reaffirming our full-year guidance along these lines.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
[Operator instructions for Q&A session: Questions via phone or web, one question and follow-up please]. Our first question comes from Jordan Lee with Goldman Sachs.

Jordan Lee:
Thanks for taking my question. Congrats on the quarter. Could you elaborate on the drivers behind customer growth and how you're thinking about acquisition costs going forward?

Michael Reynolds:
Thanks, Jordan. Great question. Our active customer base grew 8% to around 185 million globally, driven by marketplace acceleration with 5 million net new sellers and strong repeat rates at 68%. Personalization via NovaRecs v2.0 contributed significantly, lifting conversions 35%. On acquisition, CAC is trending down to $25 per new NovaPrime subscriber through ROI-positive channels like offsite ads with Google Cloud. We're balancing growth with LTV focus, targeting 15%+ uplift from GenAI tools. Confident this sustains momentum.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Rivera with JPMorgan.

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, and congrats on a strong quarter, team. I wanted to dive into fulfillment costs specifically. Fulfillment cost per order came in at $7.42, down 12% year-over-year—impressive given the macro pressures on carrier rates. Can you unpack the trends there, any efficiency levers you're pulling, and how sustainable these gains are regionally?

Sarah Chen:
Great question, Alex, and thanks for the kind words. I'll walk you through our fulfillment cost per order—or FCPO, as we track it—trends and the efficiency playbook that's driving these improvements. This is a core lever for our operating model here at NovaRetail, where we're scaling GMV while pushing adjusted EBITDA margins toward 15%. 

First, the headline trends. In Q1, FCPO landed at $7.42, a 12% decline from $8.43 in Q1 last year and a sequential 4% drop from Q4. On a two-year stack, that's a cumulative 22% improvement, outpacing our GMV growth. For context, this is against USPS and UPS surcharges up 8-10% industry-wide. Our AOV held steady around $92, so these aren't just volume effects; it's real unit economics.

Drilling into components: pick-and-pack costs fell 15% YoY to $2.18 per order, outbound shipping dropped 11% to $3.65, returns handling improved 18% to $1.02. Inbound held flat at $0.57. Labor as % of FCPO now under 28%, down from 35% two years ago.

Efficiency improvements: We've deployed over 1,200 autonomous mobile robots—customized with SwarmLogic orchestration—across 85% of our 45 North American centers. This boosted pick rates from 150 to 285 units per labor hour, 90% uplift. In mega-hubs like Dallas-Fort Worth, we're at 350 picks with AI-vision for irregular SKUs.

Tech side: ML-powered demand sensing integrated with Shopify backend cuts overstock 22%. Dynamic carrier routing via OptiShip shaved 9% off outbound, enabling 97% on-time 2-day deliveries.

Regionally: North America (72% GMV) at $6.95 FCPO with micro-fulfillment centers enabling same-day for 35% orders. Europe at $9.12 due to returns, but clawing back via automation. APAC at $8.76, improved by Singapore hub.

Guiding FCPO to $7.10-$7.30 FY24, with $450M capex on robotics, AI, EVs. Sustainability cuts dunnage 7%, boosts NPS. Long-term, vertical integration for international scale.

Bottom line: Fueling 250 bps gross margin expansion, building a moat.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Taylor Kim with Morgan Stanley.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you. On operations, how are you addressing supply chain disruptions' broader impact, and what's the outlook for inventory management?

David Patel:
Thanks, Taylor. Supply chain remains challenging, as Sarah detailed, with Red Sea, Panama, and port issues compressing turns to 10.8x. We've mitigated via AI optimization, robotics in 12 DCs boosting efficiency 35%, diversification to Vietnam/India, and EV fleets covering 15% last-mile. Inventory resilience with ML sensing hits 85% fill rates. Outlook: Moderating in Q2, with Q4 logistics at 13.8% of revenue. Expanding micro-hubs and drone pilots to derisk, targeting 12x turns by year-end while supporting 15% GMV growth.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Michael Reynolds for closing remarks.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
